adds.title: Manitoba government eyes human rights protection for gender expression - Global News (Winnipeg)
adds.summary: Global News Winnipeg (18 March 2025) reports the Manitoba NDP government plans to expand the province's Human Rights Code to cover gender expression - the code already prohibits discrimination based on gender identity, and Justice Minister Matt Wiebe says the change would bring Manitoba in line with most other provinces and cover preferred pronouns and outward appearance such as clothing. The amendment sits in a government bill before the legislature, to be debated later in 2025, and is welcomed by Charlie Eau, executive director of Trans Manitoba. This is the first province-specific human-rights-protection development on record for Manitoba, filling the gap the record notes for provincial-level trans law and official statements.

adds.title: Bill to mark transgender and two-spirit day passed by Manitoba legislature - Global News (Winnipeg)
adds.summary: Global News Winnipeg (30 May 2024) reports the Manitoba legislature passed a bill recognizing March 31 as Two-Spirit and Transgender Day of Visibility, brought forward by Logan Oxenham, a backbench New Democrat MLA for Kirkfield Park who is transgender. Oxenham said the day would show transgender, two-spirit and non-binary Manitobans that they are supported. The Legislative Assembly's passage gives Manitoba a dated, legislatively enacted trans-specific recognition at provincial level.

adds.title: Manitoba reaffirms support for trans community on Day of Remembrance - Global News (Winnipeg)
adds.summary: Global News Winnipeg (20 Nov 2023) reports Manitoba again raised the transgender flag in Winnipeg's Memorial Park for the Transgender Day of Remembrance - an observance the province first marked eight years earlier - this time with the flag raised by Logan Oxenham, the first openly trans man elected to the Manitoba legislature. In a statement, families minister Nahanni Fontaine and health minister Uzoma Asagwara said the government 'supports and upholds the life-saving work' of trans, two-spirit and gender-diverse Manitobans, and Brandon advocate Anastasia Gibson said the day memorializes people murdered as a result of transphobia, violence she said shows no sign of slowing. This documents Manitoba's official provincial position on trans people with dates, named officials and a local advocacy voice.

adds.title: Yukon MLAs pay tribute to transgender people Monday in the territorial legislature - Yukon News
adds.summary: Yukon News (31 March 2026) reports the Yukon Legislature marked International Transgender Day of Visibility on 30 March, with MLAs rising to speak: Yukon Party MLA Wade Istchenko (Kluane) praised 'the courage and resilience as well as the contributions and accomplishments of transgender, two-spirited, and gender-diverse Yukoners', acknowledged that 'too many people have experienced discrimination, harassment, and hate for far too long', and cited a national study showing transgender 15-17-year-olds face 7.6 times the risk of suicide attempt. The tribute is the territory's own cross-party, in-legislature acknowledgement of trans residents on record for Yukon.

adds.title: Yukon Government hears feedback on 2SLGBTQ plan - Yukon News
adds.summary: Yukon News (29 April 2025) reports the Yukon government published community feedback on its LGBTQ2S+ Action Plan, the first of two check-ins the government committed to when the plan was released in 2021. Of 302 survey respondents, 267 were eligible (165 self-identified 2SLGBTQ community members, 102 allies); 65 per cent agreed banning conversion therapy was beneficial - over 70 per cent of 2SLGBTQ respondents and 55.9 per cent of allies - while 11.7 per cent of allies and 9.7 per cent of 2SLGBTQ respondents judged the ban not beneficial. The article confirms conversion therapy was banned in Yukon in 2020, a year before it became illegal nationwide - a dated, quantitative record of a territorial official plan and an existing territorial law.

adds.title: Pride flag allegedly damaged, stolen from school prompts Yukon minister to double down - Yukon News
adds.summary: Yukon News (13 June 2024) reports a Pride flag was allegedly vandalized and stolen from Holy Family Elementary School in Whitehorse's Porter Creek neighbourhood over a weekend in June 2024, and that a replacement flag was promptly put up. In a statement issued 12 June, Yukon Education Minister Jeanie McLean reaffirmed her commitment to the territory's sexual orientation and gender identity policy (SOGI 123), saying Pride month celebrates 'the diversity that makes the Yukon vibrant and strong'. This is the concrete Yukon incident on record - vandalism of a Pride symbol at a Whitehorse school - paired with an explicit territorial-government response.

adds.title: RCMP raise concerns over name change notification in NWT legislation - Cabin Radio
adds.summary: Cabin Radio (2 June 2026) reports the NWT Legislative Assembly is taking feedback from police and the Northern Mosaic Network on proposed amendments to the Vital Statistics Act and Change of Name Act to make the legislation 'more inclusive for transgender, non-binary, gender-diverse and two-spirit people', including an option for trans and non-binary people to request that a name change not be published in the NWT Gazette. RCMP Chief Superintendent Dyson Smith asked MLAs to remove or amend the registrar general's option not to notify authorities, saying criminal records are tied to a person's legal name and officers may put themselves in danger if records are not transferred to a new name; Yellowknife North MLA Shauna Morgan pressed RCMP on verifying legal names without identification. This is the first on-record NWT territorial legislation specifically addressing transgender and non-binary people, with an identifiable police position on it.

adds.title: Inuvik hosts regional pride celebration with guests from around the world - APTN News
adds.summary: APTN (14 June 2023) reports youth from across the Western Arctic-Beaufort Delta gathered in Inuvik, NWT, for pride events focused on feeling comfortable 'in one's own gender and sexuality', including workshops with Two-Spirit Anishinaabe/Metis musician G.R. Gritt, a film screening of 'Small Town Pride', a pride parade, and a moment of silence at the Inuvik Community Greenhouse for Frank Gruben, an LGBTQ2S-community member from Aklavik missing since 2023. Seventeen regional students took part, bused in by the Beaufort Delta Education Council. This documents the NWT's northernmost community actively supporting trans and Two-Spirit youth while referencing an unresolved disappearance of an LGBTQ2S territorial resident.

adds.title: Tulita shows its support for Pride - Yellowknifer (NNSL)
adds.summary: Yellowknifer/NNSL (21 July 2025) reports Tulita, a small hamlet on the Mackenzie River in the NWT's Sahtu region, held its first-ever Pride celebration on 28 June 2025, a joint effort of Chief Albert Wright School, the hamlet administration and the local RCMP detachment, with a community barbecue, games and painting of an RCMP cruiser; Const. Matt Ryan counted more than 50 attendees and framed the day as creating 'a safe and welcoming space' for the 2SLGBTQI+ (two-spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex and additional) community. RCMP covered the food and paint while the hamlet and school provided volunteers, firewood and the venue, and organizers planned monthly inclusive school events from September. This is small-community NWT evidence of police-community partnership explicitly welcoming transgender residents.
